children: Third-quarter revenue rose as resident fees from new seniors housing communities and growth in the existing portfolio more than offset dispositions. The company recorded a larger net loss, reflecting higher operating and general and administrative expenses, including SHOP operating costs and severance and transition costs.

¹ Reported as “Total revenue”. ² Reported as “Net (loss) income attributable to common stockholders”. ³ Reported as “Net (loss) income attributable to common stockholders per share – basic and diluted”.
: The Landing and The Riviera generated $6.2 million of resident fees and services in the quarter, their first full quarter of operations.
: Segment revenue and NOI decreased modestly year over year, primarily driven by dispositions.
: Segment revenue was $6.2 million and property-level operating expenses were $5.5 million; NOI was $696,000.
: The company sold seven inpatient rehabilitation facilities to a joint venture for an aggregate purchase price of $217 million and retained a 15% interest.
